query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: CALPHAD-based modeling can be used to control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs by predicting the thermodynamic stability of constituent phases and their transformations.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs with a disordered face-centered cubic (FCC) structure
generation.intervention: CALPHAD-based modeling with key parameters: temperature range (300-1000 K), composition range (Al: 5-15 at.%, Co: 10-20 at.%, Cr: 10-20 at.%, Fe: 20-30 at.%, Ni: 10-20 at.%)
generation.structural_mediator: Thermodynamic stability of the FCC phase
generation.mechanism: Thermodynamic modeling of phase transformations using CALPHAD
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in the volume fraction of the ordered B2 phase relative to the baseline as-cast microstructure
generation.boundary: Temperature range (300-1000 K), composition range (Al: 5-15 at.%, Co: 10-20 at.%, Cr: 10-20 at.%, Fe: 20-30 at.%, Ni: 10-20 at.%)
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of the CALPHAD model and the effect of kinetic factors on phase evolution

falsification_experiment.design: Experimental validation of CALPHAD-based modeling predictions using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
measurements: Volume fraction of the ordered B2 phase
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimentally measured volume fraction of the ordered B2 phase is less than 10% relative to the baseline as-cast microstructure, the hypothesis is falsified

frame.system: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) with multiple constituent phases
frame.limitation: Uncertainty in method for controlling phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs
